cases.visibleGeometry: An irregular cluster of sharp, angular raised forms lies west of a curving track, with a few detached bumps nearby. The cluster coincides with exposed grey rock in the photograph. Similar outcrops occur around the context area.
cases.alternatives: Natural bedrock, boulders and erosion explain the irregular edges and repeated nearby forms; the linear trace is a present track.
cases.supportLimits: The model is mostly measured, with interpolated pockets inside the rough cluster. Fine edges there need original-return checks. Photographs and terrain have different dates.

cases.visibleGeometry: A curving break between rougher northern ground and a smoother southern slope crosses the patch. A narrow track follows part of this break. Small irregular bumps and shallow channels occur among trees to the north; scattered bumps also lie south. No coherent closed or rectilinear form is clear.
cases.alternatives: Natural slope transition, drainage, bedrock and tree-associated ground disturbance; the photograph shows a track along the break.
cases.supportLimits: Many small patches around trees and rough ground are interpolated. The break is mostly measured but its fine texture is uncertain; derivative layers reflect the same terrain model.

cases.visibleGeometry: Dense, evenly spaced curved ridges fill the western field; other parallel ridges occupy the upper and lower fields. Straight parcel boundaries meet a broad east-west track near the middle, with a small sharp bump at the junction. The photograph shows cultivated parcels and tree rows aligned with these traces.
cases.alternatives: Agricultural furrows, field banks, track grading, fence or tree-line disturbance explain the repeated ridges and junction bump.
cases.supportLimits: Most field surfaces are measured. Narrow boundary and vegetation strips contain interpolation, so their smallest apparent edges are less secure. The aerial image reflects a later season.

cases.visibleGeometry: Two roughly east-west boundaries frame a broad, textured strip with scattered low bumps. Regular parallel cultivation ridges lie above and below. One compact raised knob sits near the upper boundary at about [310,100], where the photograph shows exposed rock beside a track.
cases.alternatives: Field banks, track edges, cultivation, trees and natural rocks explain the visible forms. The knob has a direct exposed-rock counterpart.
cases.supportLimits: The broad surfaces are mostly measured, but the boundary strips and scattered patches include interpolation. Their fine texture should not be treated as separate evidence from the model derivatives.
